Deal stage/amount sync keeps the rollup fresh.
hard_constraints: No migration and no typed column; payloads are arbitrary JSON in records.data.
All reads and writes through the audited store, never a SQLite connection.
A feature must not edit any shared file, so a deal table cannot be a migration.
Features must not couple to fields other features write.
HTTP reads never write, so the rollup cannot be a stored metric row.

collections.crm_deal: CRM opportunity/deal mirror attached to a workspace through the envelope's existing room_id column. Open fields: crm_deal_id, name, account, stage, amount, currency, owner, team, created_at, closed_at.
collections.sales_impact_config: One record: which collections to read, field synonym overrides, the CRM integration state.

metric_semantics.population: A room is in scope only if its type normalises to 'sales' AND it has at least one live crm_deal attached. Excluded rooms are returned with a reason: not_sales or no_deal.
metric_semantics.total_pipeline_touched: sum of amount over every in-scope deal
metric_semantics.active_deals: count of in-scope deals whose stage is neither closed-won nor closed-lost
metric_semantics.active_pipeline: sum of amount over that open subset
metric_semantics.closed_won_deals: count of in-scope deals in a closed-won stage
metric_semantics.revenue: sum of amount over closed-won deals, in one report currency, with the per-currency split returned
metric_semantics.close_rate: closed_won / (closed_won + closed_lost); null rather than 0 when nothing has closed, because 0/0 is not a claim that everything was lost
metric_semantics.days_to_close: mean days from a closed deal's created date to its closed date over every closed deal; null when nothing has closed; a close date before the created date is excluded and reported
metric_semantics.stage_classification: Normalise, then match exact, then startswith, then substring, against won and lost sets, testing lost before won at each level. Unclassifiable is a bucket named unknown: counted, shown in the funnel, and outside both arms of the close-rate fraction, so a team's own stage string is never refused.
metric_semantics.engagement: buyer_views counts events classified as views; buyer_actions counts every event and therefore includes views. Both are counted only in in-scope rooms. average_buyers_per_workspace is distinct buyers over in-scope rooms. most_engaged_buyers ranks by actions, then views, then email, and carries workspaces and last_view_at. buyer_views_over_time is zero-filled inside the requested range. A buyer is identified by lowercased email.
metric_semantics.date_range: Filters the deal's created date on the deal side and the event's occurred-at on the engagement side.
metric_semantics.owner: A deal with no owner borrows its workspace's owner, and every row states owner_source so a borrowed owner is distinguishable from an unassigned one.

errors.InvalidFilter: 422, from after to or an unparseable date
errors.InvalidDeal: 422, a deal with neither crm_deal_id nor name
errors.DealConflict: 409, that crm_deal_id is already attached; returns the existing record id so the caller patches instead
errors.UnknownWorkspace: 404, the room_id does not resolve to a live room
errors.RecordNotFound: deliberately not claimed; the core app already maps it to 404 and two handlers for one type is a host-reported collision

query_filters_shared_by_every_aggregatin.from: ISO-8601 date, inclusive. Deal side: the deal's created date. Engagement side: the event's occurred_at.
query_filters_shared_by_every_aggregatin.stage: A raw stage string such as 'Closed Won' or 'closed_lost', or one of the classes won/lost/open/unknown, or a comma-separated list of either. Compared case- and separator-insensitively.
query_filters_shared_by_every_aggregatin.owner: comma-separated list, matched against the deal's own owner or its borrowed room owner
query_filters_shared_by_every_aggregatin.team: comma-separated list, matched against the deal's team
query_filters_shared_by_every_aggregatin.invalid: from after to, or either unparseable, raises InvalidFilter -> 422
query_filters_shared_by_every_aggregatin.echo: every aggregating read returns the applied filters under a 'filters' key so a tile is never read as a whole-report total

GET /report.money_shape: {currency: {pipeline_touched, active_pipeline, revenue}} for every currency seen, so a mixed-currency report is still readable
GET /report.scope_excluded_rows: {room_id, name, reason} where reason is not_sales or no_deal
GET /report.funnel_rows: {stage, class, deals, amount, revenue}, one per distinct stage present, ordered by deals desc then stage asc; the counts reconcile with the tiles
GET /report.deals_by_owner_rows: {owner, owner_source, deals, amount, won, lost, open}, ordered by amount desc then owner asc
GET /report.most_engaged_buyers_rows: {buyer, views, actions, workspaces, last_view_at}, ordered by actions desc, views desc, buyer asc
GET /report.warnings_rows: {code, message, room_id} for named completeness problems
GET /report.data_warnings_rows: {code, deal_id, message} for excluded data such as a close date before the created date

GET /report/rooms/{room_id}.reason: null when in scope, otherwise not_sales or no_deal
GET /report/rooms/{room_id}.existing_but_out_of_scope: 200 with in_scope false and a reason, never 404, because the research makes typing the room the user's first step and the page has to be able to explain it

POST /deals.request: the room is named by the room_id query parameter or by workspace_id in the body, the researched spelling; crm_deal_id identifies the deal in the CRM; every other key is optional and stored verbatim
POST /deals.unknown_keys_round_trip: any unrecognised key is stored in data and returned untouched
POST /deals.422: invalid_deal, when the body has neither crm_deal_id nor name
POST /deals.409: deal_conflict, when that crm_deal_id is already attached; body adds existing_id and existing_room_id so the client patches instead of creating a second row
POST /deals.404: unknown_workspace, when the room does not resolve to a live room

PATCH /deals/{deal_id}.request: a shallow merge patch over data; only the keys sent change
PATCH /deals/{deal_id}.derived_fields_are_not_persisted: stage_class, closed_at-as-derived and days_to_close are recomputed in the returned view only, because a stored derived copy would be a cache that goes stale

DELETE /deals/{deal_id}.behaviour: soft delete, the audited store's default, so the detachment and its audit row survive; returns {id, collection, room_id, hard: false}

GET /coverage.complete: true only when the CRM integration is connected and every Sales-typed room has at least one attached deal

GET /integration.200_when_absent: the default record with connected false, so the page renders before anything is configured

PATCH /integration.request: a shallow merge patch over the config record's data, e.g. {connected: true, provider: salesforce}
PATCH /integration.creates_on_first_write: so the endpoint works on a fresh database without a separate create route
PATCH /integration.provider_is_free_text: the research names Salesforce and HubSpot as having native integrations but defines no enum, so none is enforced

GET /vocabulary.properties_selection: the documented purpose of the sourced properties parameter: omit it and an endpoint returns only id, object and url
GET /vocabulary.constraints: the sourced 429 Too many requests rate-limit response

GET /inferences.inference_rows: {id, topic, basis, value, why, change_it, blast_radius}, one per inference in the design document's inference table

error_responses.InvalidFilter: 422 invalid_filter, from after to or an unparseable date
error_responses.DealConflict: 409 deal_conflict, that crm_deal_id is already attached
error_responses.UnknownWorkspace: 404 unknown_workspace, the room_id does not resolve to a live room
error_responses.RecordNotFound: deliberately not claimed; the core app already maps it to 404 and two handlers for one type is a host-reported collision

The report still answers rather than refusing, because the researched failure mode is a number that is quietly too small and a refusal would hide which rooms caused it.

Deal stage/amount sync keeps the rollup fresh. PATCH /deals/{deal_id} is that sync, a shallow merge patch, and every write passes source= built from router.prefix so the audit row names the route that actually served it.
The rollup is computed on read and writes nothing, because a stored metric row would be a cache that goes stale against a sync. HTTP reads never appear in the audit log, and a test pins that.

Registering a crm_deal_id twice is a 409 rather than a second row, so a mistyped id cannot double-count a deal in the rollup; the conflict returns the existing record id so the caller patches instead.

collections.activity: Read. The product's buyer view/action record. The collection name is configured in sales_impact_config.collections.engagement, defaulting to 'activity', not hard-coded.

data_model.envelope: id, collection, room_id, revision, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at is the only fixed vocabulary. find() and ?where= resolve dotted JSON paths through the dynamic index, so filtering on stage or crm_deal_id needs no migration.
data_model.field_discovery: Every field is located by a synonym list (stage, amount, owner, team, created, closed, currency, person, action, occurred_at) configurable in sales_impact_config.fields. A deal missing all of them is still stored, counted and shown; nothing is a required field.

metric_semantics.population: A room is in scope only if its type normalises to 'sales' AND it has at least one live crm_deal attached. Excluded rooms are returned with a reason: not_sales or no_deal. A deal on an excluded room contributes to nothing, including engagement counts, because the report is a join and a view in a room with no deal is not evidence the room moved pipeline.
metric_semantics.total_pipeline_touched: sum of amount over every in-scope deal
metric_semantics.active_deals: count of in-scope deals whose stage is neither closed-won nor closed-lost
metric_semantics.active_pipeline: sum of amount over that open subset
metric_semantics.closed_won_deals: count of in-scope deals in a closed-won stage
metric_semantics.revenue: sum of amount over closed-won deals, in one report currency, with the per-currency split returned and a warning when deals span more than one
metric_semantics.close_rate: closed_won / (closed_won + closed_lost); null rather than 0 when nothing has closed, because 0/0 is not a claim that everything was lost
metric_semantics.days_to_close: mean days from a closed deal's created date to its closed date over every closed deal; null when nothing has closed; a close date before the created date is excluded and reported in data_warnings
metric_semantics.amount_handling: A deal with no amount contributes to the counts and 0 to the sums. A deal with no currency joins the report currency.
metric_semantics.report_currency_rule: the single distinct currency if there is one, otherwise the currency on the most deals, ties broken lexicographically for determinism
metric_semantics.stage_classification: Normalise (lowercase, separators to one space, trim), then match exact, then startswith, then substring, against the won and lost sets, testing lost before won at each level. Unclassifiable is a bucket named unknown: counted, shown in the funnel, and outside both arms of the close-rate fraction, so a team's own stage string is never refused.
metric_semantics.stage_sets: Won and lost sets cover Salesforce (Closed Won, Closed Lost), HubSpot (closedwon, closedlost) and the underscore/camel/space spellings, and are configurable in sales_impact_config.fields.stage.
metric_semantics.engagement: buyer_views counts events classified as views; buyer_actions counts every event and therefore includes views, because the researched gloss of an action is interacting with a space, which is clicking into a page. Both are counted only in in-scope rooms. average_buyers_per_workspace is distinct buyers over in-scope rooms, null when there are none. most_engaged_buyers ranks by actions, then views, then email, and carries workspaces and last_view_at. buyer_views_over_time is zero-filled inside the requested range so a quiet week is not invisible. A buyer is identified by lowercased email.
metric_semantics.date_range: Filters the deal's created date on the deal side and the event's occurred-at on the engagement side, so one range, two populations, each ranged on the date that means something for it.
metric_semantics.owner: A deal with no owner borrows its workspace's owner, and every row states owner_source in deal | room | unassigned so a borrowed owner is distinguishable from a genuinely unassigned one.
metric_semantics.determinism: Every list the report returns is ordered by an explicit key, never by dict or database iteration order.

layout: Coverage banner first, naming why the report may be incomplete and listing the rooms, because the researched failure mode is a number that is quietly too small.

not_built: Calling the vendor API, because the research documents no schema for it. The properties selection and the 429 constraint are served as documented constraints at /vocabulary.

user_flow: 1. Ensure sales workspaces are typed 'Sales' and have a CRM opportunity attached (Settings, workspace Internal tab).
2. Open Reports -> Sales Impact.
3. Read the Sales Impact tiles: Total deals, Total pipeline touched, Active deals, Active pipeline, Closed won deals, Revenue, Close rate, Days to close.
4. Read Deals Created Over Time and Deals By Owner.
5. Read Buyer Engagement: Buyer Views, Buyer Actions, Buyer Views Over Time, Most Engaged Buyers.

state.data_flow: Buyer engagement in Sales-type workspaces plus CRM opportunity/deal objects feed a pipeline-weighted rollup (pipeline touched, close rate, average days to close) that a leader reads to judge whether engagement correlates with revenue outcomes. A deal whose created date is absent is never excluded by the range; it is kept and reported in data_warnings as unranged_deal, because dropping it would silently shrink a total.
query_filters.stage: A string or a comma-separated list. Each entry is either a raw stage string such as 'Closed Won', 'closed_lost' or 'negotiation', matched against the deal's stage text after case- and separator-insensitive normalisation, or one of the classes won/lost/open/unknown, matching every deal classified into it. An entry is never both kinds.
query_filters.owner: comma-separated list, matched against the resolved owner, which is the deal's own owner when it has one and otherwise its borrowed workspace owner
query_filters.team: comma-separated list, matched against the deal's team, normalised the same way
query_filters.actor: string, write routes only, recorded on the audit row
query_filters.limit: integer 1-1000, default 100, on /deals and /buyers only. Aggregated figures are always computed over the whole filtered population, never over the page, so paging can never change a total.
query_filters.invalid: from after to, or either unparseable, raises InvalidFilter -> 422
query_filters.unknown_params: ignored rather than rejected, so a client written against a newer vocabulary degrades instead of breaking

GET /report.money_shape: {currency: {pipeline_touched, active_pipeline, revenue}} for every currency seen, so a mixed-currency report is still readable
GET /report.scope_excluded_rows: {room_id, name, reason} where reason is not_sales or no_deal
GET /report.funnel_rows: {stage, class, deals, amount, revenue}, one per distinct stage present, ordered by deals desc then stage asc; the counts reconcile with the tiles
GET /report.deals_by_owner_rows: {owner, owner_source, deals, amount, won, lost, open}, ordered by amount desc then owner asc
GET /report.most_engaged_buyers_rows: {buyer, views, actions, workspaces, last_view_at}, ordered by actions desc, views desc, buyer asc
GET /report.warnings_rows: {code, message, room_id} for named completeness problems
GET /report.data_warnings_rows: {code, deal_id, message} for excluded data such as a close date before the created date

GET /report/rooms/{room_id}.reason: null when in scope, otherwise not_sales or no_deal

POST /deals.request: the room is named by the room_id query parameter or by workspace_id in the body, the researched spelling; crm_deal_id identifies the deal in the CRM; every other key is optional and stored verbatim
POST /deals.unknown_keys_round_trip: any unrecognised key is stored in data and returned untouched
POST /deals.422: invalid_deal, when the body has neither crm_deal_id nor name
POST /deals.409: deal_conflict, when that crm_deal_id is already attached; body adds existing_id and existing_room_id so the client patches instead of creating a second row
POST /deals.404: unknown_workspace, when the room does not resolve to a live room

PATCH /deals/{deal_id}.request: a shallow merge patch over data; only the keys sent change; any key from the field table may be sent; a key sent as JSON null is stored as null, which is how a field is cleared

DELETE /deals/{deal_id}.behaviour: soft delete, the audited store's default, so the detachment and its audit row survive; returns {id, collection, room_id, hard: false}

GET /coverage.complete: true only when the CRM integration is connected and every Sales-typed room has at least one attached deal

GET /integration.200_when_absent: the default record with connected false, so the page renders before anything is configured

PATCH /integration.request: a shallow merge patch over the config record's data, e.g. {connected: true, provider: salesforce}; the record is created on first write and that create is the audited write, so the first call produces an insert audit row and later calls produce update rows
PATCH /integration.provider_is_free_text: the research names Salesforce and HubSpot as having native integrations but defines no enum, so none is enforced

GET /vocabulary.properties_selection: the documented purpose of the sourced properties parameter: omit it and an endpoint returns only id, object and url
GET /vocabulary.constraints: the sourced 429 Too many requests rate-limit response

GET /inferences.inference_rows: {id, topic, basis, value, why, change_it, blast_radius}, one per inference in the design document's inference table

automations: CRM integration must be on and deals attached, or the report is incomplete. The design surfaces this as a coverage panel naming every Sales-typed room with no deal and every room that is not Sales-typed, sets complete: false, and adds a warning row. The report still answers rather than refusing, because the researched failure mode is a number that is quietly too small and a refusal would hide which rooms caused it.

Deal stage/amount sync keeps the rollup fresh. PATCH /deals/{deal_id} is that sync, a shallow merge patch, and every write passes source= built from router.prefix so the audit row names the route that actually served it.
The rollup is computed on read and writes nothing, because a stored metric row would be a cache that goes stale against a sync. HTTP reads never appear in the audit log, and a test pins that.

Registering a crm_deal_id twice is a 409 rather than a second row, so a mistyped id cannot double-count a deal in the rollup; the conflict returns the existing record id so the caller patches instead.

automations: CRM integration must be on and deals attached, or the report is incomplete. The design surfaces this as a coverage panel naming every Sales-typed room with no deal and every room that is not Sales-typed, sets complete: false, and adds a warning row. The report still answers rather than refusing, because the researched failure mode is a number that is quietly too small and a refusal would hide which rooms caused it.

Deal stage/amount sync keeps the rollup fresh. PATCH /deals/{deal_id} is that sync, a shallow merge patch, and every write passes source= built from router.prefix so the audit row names the route that actually served it.
The rollup is computed on read and writes nothing, because a stored metric row would be a cache that goes stale against a sync. HTTP reads never appear in the audit log, and a test pins that.

Registering a crm_deal_id twice is a 409 rather than a second row, so a mistyped id cannot double-count a deal in the rollup; the conflict returns the existing record id so the caller patches instead.

collections.crm_deal: The CRM opportunity/deal mirror, attached to a workspace through the record envelope's existing room_id column. Open fields: crm_deal_id, name, account, stage, amount, currency, owner, team, created_at, closed_at, close_date. Any field the CRM sends is stored verbatim in data and returned untouched.
collections.sales_impact_config: One record keyed 'default': collections to read, field synonym overrides, the won/lost stage sets, and integration {provider, connected, connected_at}.
collections.room: Read. Only the schema-flexible 'type' field, set by a team, gates inclusion; compared case- and separator-insensitively.
collections.activity: Read. The product's buyer view/action record. The collection name is configured in sales_impact_config.collections.engagement, defaulting to 'activity', not hard-coded.

data_model.envelope: id, collection, room_id, revision, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at is the only fixed vocabulary. find() and ?where= resolve dotted JSON paths through the dynamic index, so filtering on stage or crm_deal_id needs no migration.
data_model.field_discovery: Every field is located by a synonym list (stage, amount, owner, team, created, closed, currency, person, action, occurred_at) configurable in sales_impact_config.fields. A deal missing all of them is still stored, counted and shown; nothing is a required field.

metric_semantics.population: A room is in scope only if its type normalises to 'sales' AND it has at least one live crm_deal attached. Excluded rooms are returned with a reason: not_sales or no_deal. A deal on an excluded room contributes to nothing, including engagement counts, because the report is a join and a view in a room with no deal is not evidence the room moved pipeline.
metric_semantics.total_pipeline_touched: sum of amount over every in-scope deal
metric_semantics.active_deals: count of in-scope deals whose stage is neither closed-won nor closed-lost
metric_semantics.active_pipeline: sum of amount over that open subset
metric_semantics.closed_won_deals: count of in-scope deals in a closed-won stage
metric_semantics.revenue: sum of amount over closed-won deals, in one report currency, with the per-currency split returned and a warning when deals span more than one
metric_semantics.close_rate: closed_won / (closed_won + closed_lost); null rather than 0 when nothing has closed, because 0/0 is not a claim that everything was lost
metric_semantics.days_to_close: mean days from a closed deal's created date to its closed date over every closed deal; null when nothing has closed; a close date before the created date is excluded and reported in data_warnings
metric_semantics.amount_handling: A deal with no amount contributes to the counts and 0 to the sums. A deal with no currency joins the report currency.
metric_semantics.report_currency_rule: the single distinct currency if there is one, otherwise the currency on the most deals, ties broken lexicographically for determinism
metric_semantics.stage_classification: Normalise (lowercase, separators to one space, trim), then match exact, then startswith, then substring, against the won and lost sets, testing lost before won at each level. Unclassifiable is a bucket named unknown: counted, shown in the funnel, and outside both arms of the close-rate fraction, so a team's own stage string is never refused.
metric_semantics.stage_sets: Won and lost sets cover Salesforce (Closed Won, Closed Lost), HubSpot (closedwon, closedlost) and the underscore/camel/space spellings, and are configurable in sales_impact_config.fields.stage.
metric_semantics.engagement: buyer_views counts events classified as views; buyer_actions counts every event and therefore includes views, because the researched gloss of an action is interacting with a space, which is clicking into a page. Both are counted only in in-scope rooms. average_buyers_per_workspace is distinct buyers over in-scope rooms, null when there are none. most_engaged_buyers ranks by actions, then views, then email, and carries workspaces and last_view_at. buyer_views_over_time is zero-filled inside the requested range so a quiet week is not invisible. A buyer is identified by lowercased email.
metric_semantics.date_range: Filters the deal's created date on the deal side and the event's occurred-at on the engagement side, so one range, two populations, each ranged on the date that means something for it.
metric_semantics.owner: A deal with no owner borrows its workspace's owner, and every row states owner_source in deal | room | unassigned so a borrowed owner is distinguishable from a genuinely unassigned one.
metric_semantics.determinism: Every list the report returns is ordered by an explicit key, never by dict or database iteration order.

tests.domain: stage classification across both CRMs and the three match levels; lost-before-won ordering; the close-rate fraction including the 0/0 case; days-to-close including the negative-interval exclusion; currency selection and the mixed-currency warning; view versus action counting; owner fallback and owner_source; filter parsing and every rejection path.
tests.rollup: the population gate and its two exclusion reasons; that an excluded room's deal contributes to nothing including engagement; the coverage panel and the complete flag; funnel totals reconciling with the tiles; time-series zero-filling; determinism of every ordering.
tests.http: every route through this feature's own router; the four error statuses and their bodies; 404 for an unknown workspace; 200-with-reason for an existing but out-of-scope room; reads never appearing in the audit log; a schema-flexibility round trip of an unknown field.
tests.audit: every write is audited; every audit row this feature's HTTP layer produces names a route the host actually mounted, matched against the live /api/features route table; and the no-dsr.api-import guard.

user_flow: 1. Ensure sales workspaces are typed 'Sales' and have a CRM opportunity attached (Settings, workspace Internal tab).
2. Open Reports -> Sales Impact.
3. Read the Sales Impact tiles: Total deals, Total pipeline touched, Active deals, Active pipeline, Closed won deals, Revenue, Close rate, Days to close.
4. Read Deals Created Over Time and Deals By Owner.
5. Read Buyer Engagement: Buyer Views, Buyer Actions, Buyer Views Over Time, Most Engaged Buyers.
6. Filter by date range, CRM stage, owners, teams.
state.data_flow: Buyer engagement in Sales-type workspaces plus CRM opportunity/deal objects feed a pipeline-weighted rollup (pipeline touched, close rate, average days to close) that a leader reads to judge whether engagement correlates with revenue outcomes. The rollup is computed on read from records a team already keeps and writes no metric rows, because a stored metric row would be a cache that goes stale against a CRM sync.

query_filters.accepted_by: every aggregating read: GET /report, GET /report/rooms/{room_id} (as a report over one room), GET /deals, GET /buyers, GET /engagement. Every one is echoed back under a 'filters' key so a tile is never read as a whole-report total.

query_filters.stage: A string or a comma-separated list. Each entry is either a raw stage string such as 'Closed Won', 'closed_lost' or 'negotiation', matched against the deal's stage text after case- and separator-insensitive normalisation, or one of the classes won/lost/open/unknown, matching every deal classified into it. An entry is never both kinds.
query_filters.owner: comma-separated list, matched against the resolved owner, which is the deal's own owner when it has one and otherwise its borrowed workspace owner
query_filters.team: comma-separated list, matched against the deal's team, normalised the same way
query_filters.actor: string, write routes only, recorded on the audit row
query_filters.limit: integer 1-1000, default 100, on /deals and /buyers only. Aggregated figures are always computed over the whole filtered population, never over the page, so paging can never change a total.
query_filters.invalid: from after to, or either unparseable, raises InvalidFilter -> 422
query_filters.unknown_params: ignored rather than rejected, so a client written against a newer vocabulary degrades instead of breaking

Only an operator-TYPED URL that is over-long or malformed is refused. Rationale: the operator never asked for a URL, so nothing they requested is impossible; refusing would strand them over a field they left blank. Two rooms with the same 200-character prefix can then collide, which the existing '-2' suffix rule already resolves.
candidate_solutions.refuse_and_ask_for_a_shorter_url: Keep the refusal, and change the message so it tells the operator to type a shorter Friendly URL. Rationale: the URL is the room's public address, so a truncated one is a surprising, possibly unrecognisable slug; surfacing the constraint is honest. Cost: a long room name cannot be created at all without the operator doing extra work, and the research describes the URL as optional.
candidate_solutions.bound_the_name_by_the_url_limit: Reject any name whose slug would exceed the URL limit, i.e. make the effective name limit about 64 characters instead of 200. Rationale: one rule, no truncation, and the wizard's step-3 field is visibly bounded. Cost: a legitimate long room name is refused for a reason about a field the operator did not fill in, and the step-3 field's real limit becomes 64 rather than the documented 200.

context.existing_behaviour: Suffixed derived URLs are ALREADY truncated to fit the limit (base[: 64 - len(suffix) - 1] + '-' + suffix), so the code already accepts a truncated derived slug in the collision case and refuses it in the non-collision case. That inconsistency is itself a smell.
context.collision_rule: A derived URL that is taken gets a numeric suffix until free; an operator-typed URL that is taken is a 409 conflict rather than a silent rewrite.
constraints: The Friendly URL must remain a valid lowercase-hyphenated slug.

No migration may be added; the field is schema-flexible JSON.

# WF-001 - Create a Digital Sales Room from an account and template

- **Domain:** Room experience and content (`room-experience`)
- **Research source:** `docs/research/raw/room-experience.md` section 1
- **Distinct sources cited:** 5
- **Branch:** `feature/WF-001-create-a-digital-sales-room-from-an-account`

## Research evidence

- **name:** Create a room from an account and template
- **user_flow:**
  1. Open *Global Menu* → *Commerce* → *Digital Sales Room Management* (the Launchpad console).
  2. Click *Rooms* in the left sidebar.
  3. Click *New Digital Sales Room*.
  4. Wizard step 1: **select the Liferay account** to associate with the room. This account "determines the team members and contacts available to invite."
  5. Click *Next*.
  6. Wizard step 2: **select a template** ("Use the pre-configured DSR template to get started; you can customize the layout later").
  7. Click *Next*.
  8. Enter a **Name** for the room.
  9. (Optional) Enter a **Friendly URL**.
  10. Click *Save*. The room appears in the Rooms list.
- **data_flow:** Liferay Account (membership graph of internal team members + contacts) + DSR Template (a page-template/site-page definition) + operator input (name, friendly URL) → a **new DSR entry bound to a newly created Liferay site** (one site per room; the site is what later supplies the "Site ID" integration key) → appears in the Rooms list. The account binding is what makes invite-by-email work without a separate directory lookup.
- **data_sources:**
  - Liferay **Account** object (`learn.liferay.com/.../security-and-administration/users-and-permissions/accounts`)
  - Liferay **Site** (Liferay sites are the container; docs later expose a read-only `Site ID` on Room Settings)
  - DSR Template set shipped with the app

state.document:
# WF-001 — Create a Digital Sales Room from an account and a template

- **Ticket:** WF-001
- **Research:** [`docs/research/digital-sales-room-workflows/wf/WF-001.md`](research/digital-sales-room-workflows/wf/WF-001.md)
- **Source branch read as a specification:** `feature/WF-001-create-room-from-template`
- **Feature id:** `wf-001-room-templates` · **Prefix:** `/api/wf-001`

## What the research says happens

An operator opens the sales-room console, clicks *New Digital Sales Room*, and gets a
three-step wizard:

1. **Select the account** to associate with the room. The account "determines the team
   members and contacts available to invite."
2. **Select a template.** "Use the pre-configured DSR template to get started; you can
   customize the layout later."
3. **Enter a name**, optionally a **Friendly URL**, and **Save**. The room appears in the
   Rooms list.

The data flow is what shapes this implementation: the result is "a new DSR entry bound to
a newly created Liferay site (one site per room; the site is what later supplies the
'Site ID' integration key)." Two consequences:

- **The account binding is load-bearing.** It is what makes invite-by-email resolve
  without a separate directory lookup, so `account_id` is a first-class field on the
  room, resolved against a live `account` record rather than taken on trust.
- **Template identity is a pair.** The vendor inventory API the research cites returns
  `digitalSalesRoomTemplateId` *and* `digitalSalesRoomTemplateVersionId`, so a room pins
  a specific version of the template it was created from.

No public vendor API is documented for the create action itself, and none is used. The
read-side inventory API is noted in the research as something a third party calls *after*
rooms exist; it is out of scope here (see [Not in scope](#not-in-scope)).

## Design

### Storage: no new columns, no migration

Everything is a record in the existing open-JSON `records` table, written through
`AuditedDatabase`. **No migration and no typed column was added.** The fields the workflow
itself needs are documented below and are filterable through the dynamic index, so no team
needs to coordinate to add a field of their own.

`room` record `data`:

| Field | Why it exists |
|-------|---------------|
| `name` | Operator input, shown to the buyer. |
| `status` | `active` or `archived`; the Rooms list filters on one at a time and defaults to Active. See [Room state](#room-state-and-why-this-module-is-not-rooms). |
| `account_id`, `account_name` | The account binding. `account_id` is the reference; `account_name` is denormalised so the list does not need a join. |
| `template_id`, `template_version_id` | The pinned template pair. |
| `template_name`, `template_source` | `shipped` or `store`, for display. |
| `friendly_url`, `friendly_url_source` | The URL, and whether the operator typed it or it was derived. |
| `site_id` | The read-only Site ID integration key. |
| `created_by`, `created_by_username` | Matches the fields the vendor inventory API returns. |

`site` record `data`: `name`, `friendly_url`, `status`, `template_id`. The site is written
with `room_id` set, which is what makes "one site per room" queryable.

`account` and `template` records are ordinary schema-flexible records — the seed writes
`domain`, `tier`, `member_count`, `contact_count` on accounts, and a team can write
whatever else it likes.

### Room state, and why this module is not `rooms`

The source branch put this in `backend/dsr/rooms.py`. **WF-005 also adds that file**, and
it was decided, by measurement and confirmed by Jev, that **WF-005 keeps the name**: it is
the larger module and defines the room *state machine* — `RoomWorkflow`, `status_of`,
`available_actions`, `capabilities_for`, `Principal` — which is a room's own vocabulary.

So this workflow owns `backend/dsr/room_templates.py` and deliberately does **not** import
a room's status vocabulary from a module that does not exist yet. The two `status` values
here are this workflow's own field on its own record, kept so the Rooms list has something
to filter on. They are not a state machine: there are no transitions here, and WF-005 owns
those. A team that wants a third status writes a record and a filter of their own without
coordinating with anyone, which is what the schema-flexible layer is for.

### Atomicity: one transaction, two records

A room and its site must not be able to half-exist. `AuditedDatabase` gained a
`transaction()` context manager that yields an `AuditedWriter`; the room and the site are
written through that one handle, so either both records and both audit rows commit or
neither does.

That capability was **promoted into the host deliberately**, as a labelled
`platform-change` with its tests: PR #41, commit `182f56e`, merged and verified on
`main`. This branch only uses it. It does not edit `audited.py`.

This was originally **decided by Jev, not by taste** (`choose_approach`, audit
`jev-20260925T214101-11156-61605`, confidence 0.80, margin 0.74 over the runner-up), which
chose extending the audited wrapper over collapsing everything into the room record or
writing the two records sequentially.

Three details that fall out of it:

- The room id and site id are minted from one random token inside the block, so the room's
  `site_id` and the site that serves it cannot drift apart.
- Friendly-URL resolution happens **inside** the transaction, so the uniqueness check and
  the insert share one write lock and two operators cannot claim the same URL by racing.
- Each write still produces its own audit row, stamped with the same `request_id`, so one
  wizard submission reads back as a unit via `db.audit(request_id=...)`.

### Template catalogue: shipped set overlaid with the store

The research says the template set is "shipped with the app", but this project requires
that a team can add an entity without a deploy. **Decided by Jev** (audit
`jev-20260925T214101-11156-61939`, confidence 0.99): ship a module-level catalogue of
three built-in templates and overlay any `template` records on top at read time, store
records winning on `template_id` collision.

So a fresh deployment has something to select, and `POST /api/records/template` adds or
retunes a template with no code change. A store template needs only `template_id`;
`template_version_id` falls back to the id.

### Validation and failure

| Condition | Code | Status |
|-----------|------|--------|
| Empty or >200-char name | `invalid_name` | 400 |
| `account_id` missing, not an `account`, or soft-deleted | `account_not_found` | 404 |
| `template_id` not in the catalogue | `template_not_found` | 400 |
| Operator-typed URL that normalises to nothing, is not `lowercase-words-hyphenated`, or is >64 chars | `invalid_friendly_url` | 400 |
| Operator-supplied friendly URL already in use | `friendly_url_taken` | 409 |
| `status` outside `active`/`archived`/`all` on the list | `invalid_status` | 400 |

**An operator-supplied friendly URL that collides is an error, not a silent rewrite** —
rewriting what someone typed would put the room at an address they did not ask for. A URL
*derived* from the name has no such intent, so it gets a numeric suffix (`-2`, `-3`, …)
until free.

Every refusal happens before or inside the transaction, so a refused request writes
nothing: no record, no audit row.

### One correction to the branch: a long name is creatable

**The branch refused the whole creation when a valid room name produced a slug longer than
the 64-character Friendly URL limit** (`invalid_friendly_url`, "friendly URL must be at most
64 characters"). That makes a 200-character room name impossible to create, over a field
the operator never touched — and the research is explicit that the Friendly URL is
*optional*. The branch was also inconsistent with itself: the *suffixed* candidates were
already truncated to fit, so the same name could be created once its URL collided and not
created when it did not.

**Decided by Jev** (`choose_approach`, audit `jev-20260927T140106-864-66335`, confidence
**0.99**, margin 1.00 over the runner-up) against refusing the creation and against
lowering the name limit to the URL limit:

* A **derived** slug is **truncated** at 64 characters, with any trailing hyphen the cut
  leaves trimmed. Two long names sharing a 64-character prefix still get distinct URLs via
  the existing suffix rule.
* An **operator-typed** URL that is over-long or malformed is still **refused**. They asked
  for that address, so handing them a different one silently is the failure mode worth
  avoiding.

The wizard's preview says which of the two it will do, rather than promising an address the
server may not use.

### API

| Route | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `GET /api/wf-001/room-templates` | Step 2. Shipped catalogue overlaid with store records. |
| `GET /api/wf-001/accounts?q=` | Step 1. Returns account records untouched, so a team's own fields survive. |
| `POST /api/wf-001/rooms?actor=&request_id=` | Steps 1–3. Requires `name`, `account_id`, `template_id`; optional `friendly_url`, `created_by`, `created_by_username`. **Every other field is stored and indexed as-is.** |
| `GET /api/wf-001/rooms?status=&q=&account_id=&template_id=&limit=&offset=` | The Rooms list. `status` defaults to `active`. |

The generic `/api/records/*` routes are unchanged and remain the way to query arbitrary
JSON paths (`?where={"branding.theme":"dark"}`). `/api/wf-001/rooms` deliberately speaks
only the list's own filters rather than pretending to be a general query surface.

Free-text `q` is matched in Python over at most 1000 records, because the dynamic index
answers exact matches only. This is a deliberate, bounded limitation.

`RoomCreationError` carries the status and the machine-readable code; the feature exports
it in `EXCEPTION_HANDLERS` and the host attaches it, because FastAPI accepts exception
handlers on the app object only.

### `source` is a required argument, not a constant

The branch hard-coded `source="POST /api/rooms"` inside the domain module. Under the host
that route does not exist, so every audit row this workflow writes would have named a path
nobody can call — in the one table the product promises is complete. `source` is now a
required keyword on `create_room`, and the router builds it from its own `router.prefix`
via `_source()`, so the two cannot drift.

### UI

`frontend/src/features/wf-001/room-templates/` is the researched wizard: a `Stepper` (with
`aria-current="step"`), three steps, and the list below with a search box and a Status
filter defaulting to Active.

Two primitives were built here rather than added to `components/ui.jsx`, which is shared
and refused:

- `Stepper` — real `<ol>` items so position is announced.
- `ChoiceCard` — a real `<input type="radio">` inside its own `<label>`, so arrow-key
  navigation and group semantics work for free, the whole 44px card is the touch target,
  and the focus ring is drawn on the card via `has-[:focus-visible]`.

Both are **promotion candidates**: an integrator should move them into `ui.jsx` once, as
platform work, rather than every port keeping a copy. Several ports have now built their
own, which is the evidence for that platform change. The `check` and `back` glyphs are in
this feature's own `icons.js` and passed by path, so `PATHS` is untouched.

**A refused save sends the operator back to the step that caused it** rather than stranding
them on a form that cannot succeed. The shared `apiRequest` hands the page a status and the
server's operator-facing message but not the machine-readable code, and recovering that
would mean either editing `lib/api.js` — refused — or reaching around the client with a raw
`fetch`, which is the same coupling in disguise. The status is enough: **404** is
`account_not_found` and only ever that, so step 1; **409** is `friendly_url_taken`, a
step-3 field; **400** covers `invalid_name`, `invalid_friendly_url` and
`template_not_found`, all of which are step-3 fields the operator can see and fix, because
steps 1 and 2 are chosen from lists the page fetched. A status the server did not describe
(500) leaves the wizard where it is rather than inventing a step.

Design-system rules honoured: no emoji as icons (inline SVG set), `min-h-11` touch targets,
visible focus rings (never removed), 200ms transitions, `prefers-reduced-motion` respected,
text contrast ≥4.5:1.

### The frontend descriptor: the brief's path, and the host's glob

The port brief names `frontend/src/features/wf-001/room-templates/index.jsx` as this
feature's file, and that is where the implementation lives. The host's glob in
`src/lib/features.js` is `../features/*/index.jsx` — exactly one folder deep — so a
descriptor two folders down is never loaded, and a descriptor that is not loaded is a page
nobody can reach.

`frontend/src/features/wf-001-room-templates/index.jsx` is therefore a one-line re-export of
the briefed module. That is what the host globs, it is what
`docs/FEATURE-CONTRACT.md` specifies, and it is what all twenty-five sibling features do.
Widening the glob instead would mean editing `lib/features.js`, which is shared and
refused, and would let any nested folder register a route. A frontend test asserts the two
are the same module, so the nav cannot silently lose the page.

### Tests

- `backend/tests/test_wf001.py` — 75 tests. The workflow: the bindings, one-site-per-room,
  version pinning, every validation path, friendly-URL rules including the truncation
  correction, atomicity (both audit rows together, a failure *after* the room insert
  leaving no room, no site and no audit row, and the JSONL mirror not describing rolled-back
  work), schema flexibility, the template overlay, the list filters, the HTTP surface, and
  the plugin-host invariants (the four prefixed routes, no core-shaped path, no import of
  `dsr.api`).
- `frontend/src/test/wf001-room-templates.test.jsx` — 23 tests. The wizard gating, the
  status-to-step mapping for a refusal, the derived-URL preview, the request payload, and
  the descriptor reaching the host.
- No change to `tools/verify_localhost.py`, which the branch extended; that file is
  tooling, not this feature's, and the HTTP surface is covered by the feature's own tests.

### Not verified in a browser

The brief for this port does not ask for browser verification, so the research document's
"Verified in localhost browser" box is left unchecked. The frontend was built
(`npm run build`) and its page is exercised under jsdom by the test file above; a
reviewer who wants the rendered page should run the browser pass.

## Automations

**None, by design.** The research is explicit that no automation runs at creation time: the
only automation in the vendor flow is a Liferay module *site initializer* that logs a
console line when the module starts, and it is not per-room.

So every effect of this workflow is a synchronous, audited write inside the request that
triggered it. There is no background job, no queue, no scheduler, and no retry loop:

- `POST /api/wf-001/rooms` performs the two writes and returns, or performs nothing and
  returns an error.
- Nothing runs later that could bring a half-created room into existence — which is the
  main reason the two writes share one transaction rather than relying on a repair step.

If a future ticket needs an automation (sending invites on creation, say), it belongs in
that ticket's design. The one affordance this workflow leaves for it is `request_id`: a
later asynchronous action can stamp the same `request_id` and be read back as belonging to
the same submission.

## Findings for the integrator, not fixed here

Three things were found while building this. None is fixed, because each is a change to a
file this branch may not touch, and each belongs to whoever owns that file.

1. **`test_features.py` leaves routes mounted on the real app.**
   `test_shared_prefix_with_disjoint_paths_is_allowed` monkeypatches the module list and
   calls the real `load_features(app)`, which does `app.include_router(router)` on the
   *shared* app. The `clean_registry` fixture restores the registry but not the route
   table, so after that test `GET /api/rooms` answers `200 {"ok": true}` for the rest of the
   session. Any later test that asks the live app what a core-shaped path returns is
   measuring that leftover, not the product. This cost a test of mine a rewrite; the fix
   is to mount those probe routers on a throwaway `FastAPI()`, as
   `test_exception_handlers_are_registered_by_the_host` already does.

2. **The SPA catch-all's `api/` guard cannot fire.** In `dsr/api.py` the catch-all is
   `@app.get("/{full_path:path}")`, so `full_path` is `"rooms"`, not `"/api/rooms"`, and
   `full_path.startswith("api/")` is never true. With a built frontend, an unknown
   `/api/...` path therefore falls through to `index.html` instead of the intended 404
   `unknown API route`. Nothing in this feature depends on it — a feature must not claim a
   core path in the first place — but a caller mistyping an API path gets HTML.

3. **`Stepper` and `ChoiceCard` are the third and fourth local copies.**
   Promoted once into `components/ui.jsx` as platform work, they stop every future wizard
   from carrying its own.

Adds backend/dsr/features/wf043_stream_crm_record_changes_into_the_roo.py exposing 28 routes on prefix /api/wf-043 with one nav entry; a 13-module domain package backend/dsr/change_stream/ holding the domain logic beside the feature rather than inside the host; four files in frontend/src/features/wf-043-stream-crm-record-changes-into-the-roo/; and backend/tests/test_wf043.py. 19 files, no shared file touched.

Three defects were found and fixed during the port, all the same shape: a value handed to code that expected something else, behind a `|| []` guard that looked like it was handling the case.

First, the page did not render at all. The Replica component received the whole response object where it expected the row array, so `(replica || []).filter` threw a TypeError and unmounted the React tree. The prop is now unwrapped at the call site like every sibling child. `npm run build` succeeded and the source-level design-floor check passed throughout; only loading the page in a browser revealed it.

Second, the labelled toggle was a 20x20 checkbox sitting beside its label rather than inside one, so the hit area was 20x20 rather than 44px. The label now wraps the control, which makes the whole row the target without changing click or focus behaviour.

Third, two badges used the shared `delete` tone for states that are absences and cautions rather than deletions: an edition that does not carry Change Data Capture, and a channel whose buffer is below the researched 3 MB. That tint measures 3.75:1 against its own background, below the 4.5:1 floor. Both now use a tone that measures, and both read more accurately.

One collision with existing work was also resolved. The build's replica collection was `crm_replica`, which WF-045's backfill engine already owns on main. Two features writing one collection is invisible to the host's route-collision check because they serve different routes, and the symptom is one feature's listing showing rows it did not write, which reads as data rather than as a defect. WF-043's own test caught it. The arriving feature takes `crm_change_stream_replica`; the neutral name stays with the feature that landed first.

decision: Which approach best resolves: The release-bar question 'evidence_measured' scores 0.11-0.23 on every feature gated since it was pinned (WF-033, WF-043, WF-058, WF-063, WF-065), while contract_compliance, audit_integrity and design_floor all score 0.84-0.95 on the same runs. state.problem: The release-bar question 'evidence_measured' scores 0.11-0.23 on every feature gated since it was pinned (WF-033, WF-043, WF-058, WF-063, WF-065), while contract_compliance, audit_integrity and design_floor all score 0.84-0.95 on the same runs. The evidence documents state their own limits (single browser engine, no screen-reader testing, synthetic clicks, code recovered from a base ~50 commits behind main) and the question scores that honesty as missing evidence. Four features landed on recorded human overrides because of it. It will block the remaining 53 workflows identically. How should the question be fixed?

candidate_solutions.rescope_the_question: Rewrite evidence_measured to ask only whether every claim that was made is backed by a measurement actually taken, and stop it penalising limits that are declared. Add a separate question for coverage depth (how much of the change was actually measured), scored on its own terms.
candidate_solutions.drop_the_question: Remove evidence_measured entirely and let the verdict question carry the judgement, since the four other questions plus a human override already cover the risk. Fewer questions, less signal to misinterpret.

state.change_summary:
The last recovered build, ported rather than merged. The recovered version predates the plugin contract: it edited api.py, db/audited.py, store.py and components/ui.jsx, all protected shared files, and it re-derived a permission model the product already had.

Superseded? No. dsr.permissions already defines the active/archived lifecycle and already gates writes on it; WF-001, WF-002, WF-003 and WF-011 all read or render the state. What was missing was anything that performs the transition, so this is the missing half of something already half-built.

Two things the recovered build had that this one deliberately does not. It wrote ARCHIVED with a capital A while the product writes lowercase and four features compare against it; status is read case-insensitively now and the vocabulary is borrowed from dsr.permissions. It carried its own Principal and role table, duplicating four roles the product already defines; those are imported instead, and a test asserts the two cannot drift.

The design worth keeping: only `status` is written. Every other consequence is derived -- the read-only gate lives in permissions, the notice is state-driven and fires on read -- so a restore has nothing to repair, which is what makes the operation reversible at all. Archive and restore share one guarded write so the guard cannot drift between directions, and both require the same `update` permission. That second half matters most: a room archived by mistake must be recoverable, so a caller who cannot archive cannot restore either.

No create, delete, comment, upload or share: those exist on other features, and duplicating them would be a second answer to the same question. 4 files: the feature module, the two-module domain package, and the test module.

Two definitions of 'archived' in one product is how archived rooms stop being read-only, so the two cannot be allowed to drift.

measurements.both_directions_need_the_same_permission: Tests assert a Viewer and a Content Contributor are refused both archiving and restoring, and that an instance admin may do both. The restore refusal is the one that matters: a room archived by mistake must be recoverable.
measurements.the_ui_cannot_offer_a_button_the_route_w: available_actions is derived from the same two rules the write path enforces, and a test asserts the state route offers 'archive' to a Room Collaborator and nothing to a Viewer.

state.document:
DECISION
A feature seeder failed CI on 2026-10-02 with "Refusal: no availability between
2026-10-03T00:00:00Z and 2026-10-04T12:00:00Z". The chosen approach was to make
seeders compute timestamps relative to `now` rather than hardcoding ISO dates,
so availability is always in the future. Rolling the dates forward was rejected:
it re-arms the same bomb (commit e5b67f0 already did that once).

INVESTIGATION
The interval in wf056 was ALREADY relative to now: it was
(now + 1 day) at midnight, 36 hours long. So the window was never in the past.
Every asset in the demo declares Mon-Fri work_days (availability.py:239 defaults
to {0,1,2,3,4}), and 36 hours from a Saturday midnight is Saturday 00:00 to
Sunday 12:00 - zero working days, zero slots. `now + 1 day` lands on a Saturday
on every Friday the seed runs. The bug is a weekday, not an expiry.

Why it survived a green suite: every wf056 seeder test used the fixed clock
NOW = 2026-09-28 09:00 UTC, a Monday. The failure only appeared through
backend/seed.py, which uses the real clock.

THE CHANGE (backend/dsr/features/wf056_...py)
1. New _demo_day(now, margin_hours=48): walks forward from now+48h to the next
   weekday (isoweekday() <= 5). Follows the pattern already in wf058's
   _future_day and wf064's _at.
2. One anchor feeds both the booking interval and the calendar blocks.
3. DEMO_CALENDAR stamps changed from absolute instants to "+0d 13:00" style
   offsets resolved via a new _stamp(spec, day) helper, so the four blocks land
   inside the window. Previously they sat on 2026-10-06/07, outside the
   2026-10-03..04 window, so they were blocking nothing - the demo had quietly
   lost the property it exists to demonstrate.
4. The 2026-01-01T09:00:00Z stamps at the "failed_offered"/"retry_refused" demo
   are deliberately NOT offered times and were left alone.

THE TESTS (backend/tests/test_wf056.py)
Seven simulated clocks covering both weekends, three Fridays and three
late-in-day clocks. Asserts the exact outcome list, that the booked meeting is
in the future, that the anchor is always a weekday, and that every block falls
inside the window.

EVIDENCE
- New tests fail on the old code: 5 failed, and exactly 3 are Fridays.
- New tests pass on the new code: 339 passed in test_wf056.py.
- Full backend suite: 9948 passed, 2 xfailed, 0 failed.
- backend/seed.py against a temp DB: no "seed FAILED", no "SKIPPED".
  wf056 -> 4 sessions: booked, failed_offered, retry_refused, booked_handoff.
- Read back from the throwaway DB via AuditedDatabase: meetings at
  2026-10-05T09:00Z (+3 days from a 2026-10-02 clock); the four calendar blocks
  on 2026-10-05/06, inside the Mon 10-05 00:00 -> Tue 10-06 12:00 window.
- A sweep of all 48 seeding modules against 37 simulated clocks (21 consecutive
  days, late-in-day, 2027/2028 dates past every hardcoded stamp, Fridays in
  2027/2028/2030): 0 failures on the new code. The same sweep on the old code
  reports 11 failing clocks, every one a Friday, including 2026-10-09 and
  2026-10-16.

QUESTIONS
1. Is anchoring on the next weekday the correct root-cause fix, given the
   failure was a weekend landing inside the window rather than an expired date?
2. Is converting DEMO_CALENDAR to offsets correct, or does changing it risk
   altering what the demo demonstrates beyond the window alignment?
3. Is the margin of 48 hours sound, or too short/long for a seed that might run
   at any hour of any weekday?
4. Are the untouched sites (wf057 _slot(), wf063 DEMO_MEETINGS, and the
   2026-10-05/06/07 stamps in the test files) correctly left alone as arbitrary
   fixture data rather than seeds of the same bug?
5. Does this avoid re-arming the time bomb, or only move the expiry?

VERIFICATION
- cd backend && ../.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest  -> 9948 passed, 2 xfailed
- ../.venv/Scripts/python ../tools/check_feature_diff.py --base origin/main

# WF-014 - Expire or cap access to a room

- **Domain:** Room experience and content (`room-experience`)
- **Research source:** `docs/research/raw/room-experience.md` section 14
- **Distinct sources cited:** 9
- **Criticality:** critical (C2)
- **Why:** Being unable to end access means every link is permanent. Confidential material cannot be shared on that basis.
- **Branch:** `feature/WF-014-expire-or-cap-access-to-a-room`

## Research evidence

- **name:** Expire or cap access to a room
- **user_flow:**
  1. Click the **Share** button (from the dashboard or the page editor).
  2. Click **Link expiry settings** → enable **Enable Link Expiry** → type the number of days (or use the arrows).
  3. Optionally **Other settings** → enable **Restrict Number of Views** and enter the view count cap.
  4. *(optional)* Add password protection (`Add password protection`) for non-Growth/Scale plans.
  5. Observe: on the expiration date the page "will automatically switch to a **Declined** status" on the dashboard; when the view cap is reached the status reads **View Limit** while the page "will retain a Live status, although it's been disabled by the view limit."
  6. Buyers see a persistent message bottom-left when expiry is within 7 days, and an error message once expiry/limit is hit. To change or remove, reopen the same settings; to revive, **Share → Set Live**.
- **data_flow:** Room/page link + (expiry day count | view cap) → on reaching the cap: an error message replaces page content; on reaching the expiry date: status transition `live → declined` and the public link stops working → dashboard reflects the new state. Changeable at any time; revival via `Set Live` re-enables the link. Both are stored as first-class record fields, so `GET /v1/pages?status=…` and `?tags=archived` reflect them.
- **data_sources:**
  - Qwilr **page** record: `expiry { enabled, …days }`, view-limit setting, `status`
  - Qwilr **view counter** per page
  - Qwilr **dashboard status model** (Draft / Live / Pending / Accepted / Declined / Blueprint / View Limit)
  - No external IdP or CRM involved
- **apis_hit:**
  - `PUT https://api.qwilr.com/v1/pages/{pageId}` with `expiry` and `published` — "Updates the `published` field of the page, its link `expiry` settings and its Qwilr Pay `paymentSettings`."
  - `expiry` semantics: "When you enable expiry, the link of the page stops working after the number of days that you set, and the status of the page becomes `declined`. The count of days starts when you publish the page. A draft page keeps the setting until you publish it."
  - `GET https://api.qwilr.com/v1/pages?status=draft,live,accepting,accepted,disabled,declined` — filter by terminal status; `?tags=archived` for archived.
  - `POST https://api.qwilr.com/v1/pages` accepts `expiry` at creation.
  - Webhook events relevant to the revived case: `"pageRevivedLive"`, `"pageDeclined"` is **not** in the published event enum — the documented events are `"pageAccepted" "pagePartiallyAccepted" "pagePreviewAccepted" "pageViewed" "pageFirstViewed" "pageSetLive" "pageRevivedLive"`, so expiry-driven decline is a poll-only signal.
- **automations:**
  - **Automatic status transition on expiry:** "On the expiration date, the page will automatically switch to a Declined status."
  - **Automatic link death on cap:** "Once that number has been reached, your clients will see an error message when they view the page."
  - **Buyer-side imminent-expiry nudge:** "if the expiration date is within 7 days they'll see a persistent message in the bottom left corner."
  - **Status-on-expiry can be masked:** "The Page will retain a **Live status**, although it's been disabled by the view limit. If you'd rather mark the page as Declined, click the **Share** button…" — so `Live` does not imply accessible.
  - **Liferay's analogue** (different mechanism, same goal): per-person `Access Valid Until` with UTC cut-off and a 7-day warning banner (workflow 4), and per-room Archive/Restore (workflow 5).
- **features_tools:** Share pop-up → **Link expiry settings** (**Enable Link Expiry** + day stepper) and **Other settings** → **Restrict Number of Views**; dashboard status badges *Declined* and *View Limit*; **Share → Set Live** to revive; buyer-facing expiry banner and error page; password protection (lower plans).
- **extensibility:** Two orthogonal, independently toggleable constraints (time and count) that compose, plus a documented interaction to respect when reviving: "If your page reaches the view limit and then you manually set it as Declined, you can still manually set it Live later. If you do that, the view limit setting will still in place, so you'll want to use the steps above to remove it." Liferay supplies the third primitive (per-recipient expiry) that Qwilr lacks — a strong argument for supporting both in a room product.
- **sources:**
  - https://help.qwilr.com/article/768-setting-automatic-link-expiry-on-a-qwilr-page
  - https://help.qwilr.com/article/148-adding-view-limits
  - https://help.qwilr.com/article/578-dashboard-page-statuses
  - https://help.qwilr.com/article/151-adding-security
  - https://docs.qwilr.com/api-reference
  - https://learn.liferay.com/w/digital-sales-room/managing-rooms
- **evidence:**
  - "By default, Qwilr's public page URLs never expire. With the expiry setting, you can make the link active for a specific number of days. Once that time is up, the link will display an error message instead."
  - "On the expiration date, the page will automatically switch to a Declined status. You'll see that on your dashboard." / "You can always set the page Live once again if needed."
  - "When your client views the page, if the expiration date is within 7 days they'll see a persistent message in the bottom left corner."
  - "Enable the **Restrict Number of Views** switch, and enter the number of times your page can be viewed. Once that number has been reached, your clients will see an error message when they view the page."
  - "Once your client reaches the view limit, you'll see the status on your dashboard change to **View Limit**. The Page will retain a **Live status**, although it's been disabled by the view limit."
  - "You'll see this status on your dashboard for two reasons: The page has reached a link expiration you've set; You've manually set the page as Declined."
  - Liferay: "Access ends at the end of the expiration date in UTC. The person then no longer appears in the Who Has Access list."

---

state.domain_module_excerpt:
"""WF-014: expire or cap access to a room.

Two constraints bound a room's link, and they compose:

* **Expiry** - a number of days, counted from the moment the page goes live.
* **A view cap** - a number of times the page may be opened.

Both are independent switches. Either can be on without the other, both can be on
at once, and a room may carry both, expire first, hit its cap first, or do
neither. The research calls them out as "two orthogonal, independently toggleable
constraints (time and count) that compose", and this module keeps them orthogonal:
nothing in the expiry path reads the cap, and nothing in the cap path reads the
expiry.

The rule this module exists to get right
----------------------------------------

**A status is not a claim that a link works.** The two come apart, and the
research is explicit that they do:

    "Once your client reaches the view limit, you'll see the status on your
    dashboard change to View Limit. The Page will retain a Live status, although
    it's been disabled by the view limit."

    "...so `Live` does not imply accessible."

So a page whose badge reads ``live`` may still be closed to every buyer, and the
badge alone can never decide whether a link opens. Everything a buyer experiences
is therefore *derived on read*, from the stored window plus a fresh count, rather
than read off a status field written once and left to rot.

Deriving on read is also the only correct choice against the vendor's own event
enum, which contains no expiry signal at all:

    "pageAccepted" "pagePartiallyAccepted" "pagePreviewAccepted" "pageViewed"
    "pageFirstViewed" "pageSetLive" "pageRevivedLive"

``pageDeclined`` is not published. Expiry-driven decline is a poll-only signal. A
build that waited for an event the vendor does not send would leave an expired
page open forever, which is the failure this whole workflow exists to prevent.

What is stored, and what is not
-------------------------------

Stored on the page record under ``data.access_window``::

    {"expiry":      {"enabled": bool, "days": int | None, "starts_at": str | None},
     "view_limit":  {"enabled": bool, "max_views": int | None},
     "manual_status": "live" | "declined" | None}

Everything else - ``expires_at``, the badge, whether a buyer may in, what a buyer
is told - is derived. In particular this feature never writes the page's own
``status``: that field belongs to ``dsr.pages`` and to the editor, and its
vocabulary there is ``draft`` / ``published``. This feature answers a different
question - whether the link works right now - and it answers it without editing
another feature's field. The consequence is worth stating plainly, because it is
the kind of thing a reviewer should not have to discover from the diff: a seller
reading ``status`` off a page record still sees ``published`` for a page that
expired an hour ago. They read ``access_status`` here instead, and
``GET /api/wf-014/pages?status=`` filters on it the way the vendor's
``GET /v1/pages?status=`` filters on the dashboard badge.

Where the research left a gap
-----------------------------

Five points are inferences rather than sourced rules. Each is marked at its
definition below with the reading taken and the reason, and all five are served
over ``GET /api/wf-014/vocabulary`` so a reviewer can check the claim against the
code that enforces it rather than against this docstring.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from typing import Any

from dsr.db.audited import AuditError
from dsr.permissions import capabilities
from dsr.store import RecordStore

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Collections
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

ROOMS = "room"
PAGES = "page"

#: One row per page opening. The cap is an aggregate over this collection, which
#: is why it is counted with ``count_where`` rather than measured by loading rows
#: and taking a length.
#:
#: Deliberately not ``access_session``: that is WF-015's collection for verified
#: buyer sessions, and sharing a name would make two live features read each
#: other's rows.
PAGE_VIEWS = "page_view"

#: The key on a page's ``data`` holding this feature's configuration. Nested so
#: that enabling a cap cannot collide with a field another workflow added.
WINDOW_KEY = "access_window"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# The badge vocabulary
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

#: The page has never been published, so there is no link to open. The research
#: calls this ``draft``: "``draft`` selects the pages that you have not
#: published."
STATUS_DRAFT = "draft"

#: Published, unexpired, under its cap. The badge that most pages wear.
STATUS_LIVE = "live"

#: Published and open to buyers, but the link will stop working within
#: ``EXPIRY_WARNING_DAYS``. Not a vendor status: it is the seller-side reading of
#: the same condition the buyer sees as a warning message.
STATUS_EXPIRING = "expiring_soon"

#: Closed. Reached by expiry (automatically) or by a seller declining it by hand.
STATUS_DECLINED = "declined"

#: Published and still badged ``live``, but every buyer gets an error because the
#: cap is spent. The research is precise that the underlying status does *not*
#: change: "The Page will retain a Live status, although it's been disabled by
#: the view limit." So this is a badge, and the page's stored status is untouched.
STATUS_VIEW_LIMIT = "view_limit"

#: Every badge this feature can produce. Exposed over HTTP so a client never
#: hard-codes the list, which is how a second vocabulary starts.
ACCESS_STATUSES: tuple[str, ...] = (
    STATUS_DRAFT,
    STATUS_LIVE,
    STATUS_EXPIRING,
    STATUS_DECLINED,
    STATUS_VIEW_LIMIT,
)

#: What a buyer is doing, as opposed to what a seller's dashboard shows.
#:
#: ``open`` and ``expiring_soon`` show content. The other three replace it with an
#: error message, which is what the research describes: "Once that time is up,
#: the link will display an error message instead."
BUYER_OPEN = "open"
BUYER_EXPIRING_SOON = "expiring_soon"
BUYER_EXPIRED = "expired"
BUYER_VIEW_LIMIT = "view_limit"
BUYER_DECLINED = "declined"
BUYER_UNPUBLISHED = "unpublished"

BUYER_STATES: tuple[str, ...] = (
    BUYER_OPEN,
    BUYER_EXPIRING_SOON,
    BUYER_EXPIRED,
    BUYER_VIEW_LIMIT,
    BUYER_DECLINED,
    BUYER_UNPUBLISHED,
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Constants the research fixes
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

#: "When your client views the page, if the expiration date is within 7 days
#: they'll see a persistent message in the bottom left corner." The same seven-day

state.problem: Decide how coverage must be measured and combined under pytest-xdist with -n auto, and whether the -n auto number is trustworthy as the gated number.

candidate_solutions.pytest_cov_plus_dist: Use pytest-cov --cov=dsr with the addopts -n auto already in place. pytest-cov has workers write per-process data files and combines them in the controller. Add COV_CORE_SOURCE=dsr so coverage starts early.
candidate_solutions.coverage_run_plus_combine: Turn coverage off under xdist and run pytest-cov serially with -n 0. No combining step, but the job gives up the parallel speedup.
candidate_solutions.dist_combine_explicit: Run coverage under -n auto and add an explicit combine step such as coverage combine plus coverage json, so the report is produced by an explicit command rather than by the plugin.
candidate_solutions.pytest_cov_dist_no_core_source: Use pytest-cov --cov=dsr with the addopts -n auto, no COV_CORE_SOURCE and no extra combine step. Rely on the measurement that the xdist report equals the serial report.

context.known_trap: Under xdist, coverage started in each worker process can report only the subset one worker saw, which reads as a plausible but wrong total. The question is whether the observed numbers agree.
context.verification_performed: Two full runs of the same commit 0b57667 in the same working tree, one with -n auto and one with -n 0, both with --cov=dsr --cov-report=json. The two JSON reports were then compared file by file and uncovered line set by uncovered line set, not only by their totals. Both runs reported 11127 passed and 2 xfailed and exited 0.
context.cost_of_the_serial_option: Serial with coverage took 420.45 s on this host against 231.84 s for the same suite under -n auto with coverage. On a 4-core GitHub runner the gap is larger. Giving up xdist buys nothing here, because the xdist number already matches the serial number.
context.cost_of_coverage_itself: Under -n auto the suite took 230.65 s without coverage and 231.84 s with it. Coverage tracing cost about 1 second on 11129 tests on this host.
context.criterion: If the two reports agree then the combining is already correct and no extra step is needed. If they differ then the xdist number cannot be the gated number and the job must run coverage serially.

candidate_solutions.land_as_plugin: Copy the 8 files onto forensics-062 as a normal plugin feature and open a pull request to main. The work already follows the feature contract, its 303 tests pass against current main, and no shared file is edited.
candidate_solutions.reimplement: Throw the recovered code away and build WF-062 again from the research document. Costs the 303 passing tests and the 9 named inferences.
candidate_solutions.archive: Push the branch to archive/wf-062 with no pull request. Keeps the only copy but ships no behaviour.

context.what_this_is: A digital sales room workflow. An admin turns requires confirmation on for an event type. A prospect or agent asks for a slot. The booking is created PENDING with a oneTimePassword. A BOOKING_REQUESTED webhook fires and the rep is notified. The host confirms, which gives ACCEPTED and is the only moment a calendar event is created, or declines with a reason, which gives REJECTED. A decline fires BOOKING_REJECTED carrying rejectionReason back to the attendee, and it releases the held slot.
files_found_in_the_orphan_not_on_main: backend/dsr/booking_approval.py, 1555 lines. The pure domain: vocabulary, the state machine, authorisation, the bypass conjunction, the email verification gate, the webhook payloads. No database and no framework.
backend/dsr/features/wf062_route_a_requested_slot_for_host_approv.py, 1441 lines. The feature host module. Exports FEATURE, router on prefix /api/wf-062, EXCEPTION_HANDLERS and seed(db, context).
backend/tests/test_wf062.py, 1499 lines. 171 tests against the pure domain.
backend/tests/test_wf062_http.py, 1723 lines. 132 tests through the mounted router.
frontend/src/features/wf-062-route-a-requested-slot-for-host-approv/index.jsx. The descriptor, default export { id, label, icon, Component }.
orchestration/decisions/jev-audit.jsonl, modified. Two appended audit rows written by the Jev client itself.

the_two_findings_that_needed_judgement.F841_was_the_test_hollow: No. The test is test_a_request_records_the_actor_it_was_given_over_http. It posts a slot request with the query parameter actor=dana, then asserts that the booking_request audit row has actor 'dana'. That assertion is exactly what the test name claims, so the test is not hollow. The response body was never part of the intent because the subject of the test is the recorded actor, not the reply.
the_two_findings_that_needed_judgement.F841_proved_by_mutation: The assertion was temporarily changed to expect 'MUTANT-NOT-DANA' and the single test was run. It FAILED with 'AssertionError: assert dana == MUTANT-NOT-DANA'. The assertion is therefore load-bearing and the test would catch a regression that dropped the actor. The mutation was then reverted and the revert was verified by searching the diff for the mutant string, which found none. So dropping the unused assignment removed a leftover, not a check.
the_two_findings_that_needed_judgement.B905_which_strict_was_chosen: strict=True was chosen. The helper serves() has the docstring 'Segment by segment, because a path parameter fills exactly one segment: the two must line up in number as well as in shape.' Number-equality is stated as a requirement of the comparison, so strict=True records that requirement at the point of use.
the_two_findings_that_needed_judgement.B905_why_it_cannot_change_behaviour: The line immediately above the zip is 'if len(candidate) != len(recorded): continue'. The two sequences are therefore guaranteed to be the same length before the zip is ever reached, so strict=True can never raise. strict=False would be behaviourally identical here for the same reason. strict=True was chosen because it makes the documented precondition executable rather than implied, and it would catch a future edit that removed the length guard.
